widgets_values:
# OpenCast Studio · FLUX3 anchor → Pika video

Load a source video, one character image and optionally a background. Set **Motion transfer ON** to change the scene; OFF replaces a person while preserving the scene. Add an optional target instruction. Set High video resolution OFF for ~0.5 MP or ON for ~1 MP. The anchor stays 1 MP.

The backend normalizes input to 24 fps. When running this canvas directly, supply 24 fps video. Automatic duration uses up to 15 seconds and rounds down to the H3 17n + 5 frame grid (maximum 345 frames / 14.375 seconds). No scene-cut detection.

FLUX3 uses its official prompt upsampler, then 16 Euler/simple steps at CFG 1. Pika uses the existing six-step Flex recipe with Add Guide at frame 0. No GPT, SAM or depth model.

nodes.title: Models
widgets_values:
# Model setup

[FLUX3 model, encoder and prompt upsampler](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-comfy) · accept its access conditions, then install the three pinned files listed in Resources. The tested [FLUX2 VAE](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Flux-2-Dev) installs automatically. Store image models in diffusion_models/, encoders in text_encoders/, VAEs in vae/, and the Pika adapter in loras/.

[H3 base, text encoder and VAEs](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3) · [Pika H3 Flex adapter](https://huggingface.co/Pika-Labs/Pika-H3-Flex). Use the bundled manifest for exact filenames, folders, sizes and hashes.

ComfyUI core: 63be2f9b82ad0dac88a7ceaa28a9cf3154125a18. Native nodes only. Full dependency lock is bundled.

Separate background OFF uses the character image's setting. A neutral character sheet has no meaningful environment. Pose, framing and identity still need visual review.

widgets_values:
You are the prompt upsampler of an image-editing model. You see the reference image(s), attached in order (the first image, the second image, ...), and the user's short request. Expand it into ONE detailed, self-contained instruction: the caption the editing model receives together with the same images. Output only the instruction as one continuous English prose block, with no greetings, explanations, Markdown, JSON, coordinates, ids or angle-bracket tokens. Read a vague or conversational request as the most plausible edit of the supplied images.

Pick the voice by task shape. When one reference stays and gets bounded changes, write an imperative editing instruction on it ("Remove the ...", "Change the ... to ...", "Zoom in on ..."); a whole-image transformation opens with its scope ("Convert the entire image into ...", "Apply a ... filter over the entire scene", "Horizontally flip the entire image so that ...", "Shift the camera viewpoint to ...", then where the major elements should now be). When the references are drawn into a newly composed frame (combining subjects, a new scene, a garment, object or style donor), write a generation request ("Create a photograph of ...", "Create an anime-style illustration of ...", "Generate a new image featuring ...") that says what to take from each image, by ordinal, and what is newly generated.

Keep every explicit edit, constraint, count, position, style cue and piece of wording, and decide what is left open as one concrete plan. Ground everything in what is actually visible: identify each referent unambiguously by its real appearance, never mention content that is not there, and use every image the user attached. State every end state concretely (which color, how large, which pose, which material) and give new content enough appearance to be generated. Cover the knock-on effects of the change (shadows, reflections, occlusion, perspective, scale, lighting) and say what fills a removed region. A zoom-in names what stays in frame and which neighbors are cropped out; an outpainting continues the scene in the same medium. Describe the change, not the whole scene, and close an editing instruction with one compact clause naming what stays unchanged; transferred people keep their identity, face and accessories unless asked otherwise. Transcribe on-image text verbatim in its original language inside double quotes, with line breaks as \n, and match the original font, size and color when replacing it. Name recognizable public figures, brands and landmarks you can see. Directions are frame-relative; use no evaluative or quality words. Typical length is 50 to 150 words.

Output only the instruction.

nodes.title: MiniMax H3 Reference to Video · audio ON
Video template · motion transfer
widgets_values: References: @Image1 is the character sheet (front view of ONE character). @Image2 is the environment. @Image3 is the starting Frame 0 image that is a guide for how the exact start of the video should look. @Video1 is the motion reference only. Make a new video of the character from @Image1, inside the environment from @Image2, performing exactly the body motion, choreography, timing and camera movement of the person in @Video1. Use @Image3 as the starting frame. Take NOTHING else from @Video1 - not the person's face, body, clothes, props, location, background, colours or photographic look. Keep the character exactly as designed in @Image1 - same face, proportions, outfit, colours - and render the whole video in the exact art style of @Image1 and @Image2. Only ONE character in frame. Style: exactly as @Image1 and @Image2. Audio: same as the reference video @Video1. Normal real-time speed, NO slow motion. No text, no captions, no logos.
